summary: Fremont NF lookout on Sycan Butte, Lake County OR, built 1931, replaced 1964, staffed to 1984; tower moved to Hogback Mountain 1987-88; site now gone.

facts.design: 1931: 14x14 cabin on a timber pole tower (35 ft per register, 31 ft per local history); 1964: steel tower with wooden cab (28 ft per register, 30 ft per local history)
facts.status_note: Tower moved to Hogback Mountain in 1987 or 1988; no source describes what remains at the Sycan Butte site

events.note: First lookout built by the Fremont National Forest: 14x14 cabin on a timber tower with 50 steps
Helen Johnson named as the lookout, a Fremont National Forest employee
KFPA staffed and maintained the station, which sat on USFS land
Steel tower built next to the old one, which was kept as a gin pole; register says 28 ft, local history says 30 ft
Five fires reported from the station in 1969
Explosion and resulting fire caused major damage to the interior
Last year the lookout was staffed; register says the tower was used for an emergency that year
Register and firelookout.com date the move to Hogback Mountain to 1987
Tower re-erected on Hogback Mountain by ODF; local history, Hogback register entry, Herald and News and Hogback history date this to 1988

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives a 35 ft pole L-4 tower; local history gives a 31 ft timber tower. Story reports both figures and does not pick one.
Register says 28 ft; local history and a 1964 newspaper item say 30 ft. Story reports both.

resolved_conflicts.field: year the tower moved to Hogback Mountain
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com say 1987; local history, Hogback register entry, Herald and News and Hogback history say 1988 (the Hogback entry says the tower came the year after its 1987 condemnation). Story gives both dates and says the sources differ.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 10.7 (35 ft) is the 1931 pole tower only; the last tower on the site was 28-30 ft steel, so height_m was left out. No source describes the Sycan Butte summit today, and its access is not described; the access key is omitted. The 1942 memo cited on the local history page is not quoted here. Hogback Mountain's own first tower (NHLR says 1941; a 1947 newspaper describes a new 40-foot tower) is outside this story and was not checked further. The Herald and News photo caption mentions a gated-off section of the Hogback tower, but no source states an access rule, so the story gives no visitor advice.
